## At a glance

- **The turn.** The Party learns that the harbormaster's ledger lies in the chapel bell loft and that the Reedrunners are after it.
- **Changes.** The Party knows the route, the risk under the boards and how much time the tide gives them. They also receive the handout [[Hobb's Warning]].
- **Where.** The tally house in [[Reedholt]].
- **Who.** [[Nib Ashwater]].

> [!narration] Opening
> The tally house is long and dim, and the roof is lined with hanging sticks, thousands of them, each one notched and knotted with thread. They click softly in the draft. A stove ticks in the corner, and the air smells of cedar and damp wool. Nib closes the door behind you and stands with his back against it. "Forty-one boats since dawn," he says. "One of them was not on my list, and I think it was hers."

## Play

### Situation

Nib decided long ago to leave the ledger alone, though he knows more than he has ever said. The bell changed his mind. He will show the Party the tally-sticks if they show respect, and he will share the location of the ledger if they can say the name of one person on the sticks. [[Pell Rushlight]] arrives during the talk with a folded note from [[Hobb Tarrow]], the handout [[Hobb's Warning]].

### Handles

- **Read the sticks.** Each stick holds a family's names. [[Odalys Ferro]] can read the Vessen knots, and the names move Nib to trust the Party.
- **Ask about the ledger.** Nib says it lies "where the bell hangs" and, if trusted, describes the niche in the loft.
- **Ask about the Reedrunners.** Nib lists the boats that left Saltwick at dusk and says [[Ilse Corran]] is among them.
- **Ask about the drowned man.** Nib says the dead man wore Vessen boots and had a tally-stick in his fist.

### Checks

- Winning Nib's trust takes a DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) check, and it is automatic if the Party names someone on the sticks.
- Reading the old Vessen knots takes a DC 14 Intelligence (History) check.
- Sensible actions such as asking Nib questions, reading the letter or looking at the map succeed and yield their Clue.

## Depth

### Hidden truths

- Nib's grandmother kept a second set of sticks for the drowned because she believed someone would ask for them. The Party can learn this from the date knots on the oldest sticks.
- The drowned man on the plank walk was one of the drowners' victims, not a natural death. See [[Mire Drowner]].

### Threads

- [[The Silent Bell]]: the sticks are the only complete list of Vessen's dead.
- In [[Reedrunner Tithe]], Nib has warned the moot for years and has been ignored.

### Spotlight

- [[Odalys Ferro]] can read the Vessen knots and finds a name on the sticks that matches her order's oldest prayer.
